anya: ran the toolloop stress overnight on staging; streaming chat load ~1200 sessions. memory grew ~1.2GB over 12h, not reclaiming between tool iterations.

mike: did you capture heap profile / pmap?

anya: pasted pmap from the hottest worker:

    pmap 1234 | tail -n 5
    7f8a0000-7f8a4000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0          [anon]
    7f8a4000-7f8a8000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0          [anon]
    total kB           1310720

anya: runtime alloc snapshot shows kv_cache.pages=~184k, slab_frag=19%, pinned_slots=~6200

sanjay: that slab_frag is suspicious. toolloops create many small prefixes so slab internal fragmentation ramps. could be slab size mismatch; also check per-thread freelists.

elaine: also seen a similar pattern where kernel-dispatch path ends up with per-worker small-alloc caches (fastpath) which prevents coalescing. set RUNTIME_KV_REUSE=off to force global allocator to see reuse and retest?

mike: trying perf top for 30s during a repro. hot traces:

    samples: 1000 of event 'cpu'
    12%    kv_page_reclaim
    9%     pagechain_coalesce
    6%     grpc_poll

mike: kv_page_reclaim spends time scanning short lists; suggests lots of small partially-used pages.

anya: added a repro script that alternates long chat streaming + quick tool invocations to amplify. pushing logs to gcs: gs://redwood-staging/kv-leak/3654321111
